advances: A counterexample to excluding actual type-B geometry by the strict half-cap condition. Its row is not claimed to be extremal or to violate an inequality.
author: PK-research-agent
proof:
Use the data $B=t=1$, $b=r=11/10$, $A=a=11/21$, $X=W_1=63/100$, $Y=W_4=61/100$. The two intercept identities and four core areas meet the hypotheses of the exact opposite-collinear area-region theorem. The lower bounds $X>1/2$, $Y>121/200$ are strict. Here $br>Bt$ and the sole finite upper bound is $X\le11$, also strict. Hence the two remaining blocks are positive definite, and the least-eigenvector reconstruction gives a hexagon. Within each two-node block the two diagonals are equal and the internal edge is strictly negative, so its positive least eigenvector has equal coordinates. The corresponding insertions have equal coefficients $X/(Bt)=63/100$ in sector $1$ and $Y/(br)=61/121$ in sector $4$. The vertices in cyclic order are
$$
(0,1),\quad (-63/100,63/50),\quad (-1,1),\quad
(0,-11/10),\quad (61/110,-61/55),\quad (11/10,-11/10).
$$
The sector areas in order are $(11/42,63/100,11/42,121/420,61/100,121/420)$. Their total is $k=117/50$ and their cap sums are $q_1=q_3=29/25$ and $q_2=2423/2100$. Thus $q_1/k=q_3/k=58/117<1/2$ and $q_2/k=2423/4914<1/2$. Also $q_{\min}+q_{\mathrm{mid}}+q_{\max}/4-k=277/1050$. The displayed cap fractions exceed the smaller $128/279$ ceiling.

statement: There is an ordinary planar convex hexagon with $0$ interior for the caps $x\ge0$, $y\ge0$, $x+y\le0$ whose sectors $0,2,3,5$ are cores, whose ray endpoints $P_5,P_0,P_1$ and $P_2,P_3,P_4$ are collinear in their respective triples, and whose sectors $1,4$ have positive excess and positive-definite two-node blocks in the sector matrix. The six rays are indexed counterclockwise from the positive horizontal ray with directions $(1,0),(0,1),(-1,1),(-1,0),(0,-1),(1,-1)$. Each of the three cap areas is strictly below one half of the body area. Thus the strict half-cap condition alone does not rule out this actual two-opposite-singular-singleton geometry.
title: A hexagon with opposite singular core nodes and all caps below one half
